arXiv:2406.18339v2 [math.AP] 19 Sep 2024

Convergence to equilibrium for
a degenerate three species reaction-diffusion system

Saumyajit Das Address: S.D.: Department of Mathematics, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Powai, Mumbai 400076 India. Email address: 194099001@iitb.ac.in and Harsha Hutridurga Address: H.H.: Department of Mathematics, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Powai, Mumbai 400076 India. Email address: hutridurga@iitb.ac.in
Abstract.

In this work, we study a 3×33\times 3 triangular reaction-diffusion system. Our main objective is to understand the long time behaviour of solutions to this reaction-diffusion system when there are degeneracies. More precisely, we treat cases when one of the diffusion coefficients vanishes while the other two diffusion coefficients stay positive. We prove convergence to equilibrium type results. In all our results, the constants appearing in the decay estimates are explicit.

Key words. Reaction-Diffusion, Entropy method, Degenerate diffusion, Large time behaviour

Mathematics Subject Classification. 35K57, 35K65, 35Q92, 92E20, 39B62

1. Introduction

Reaction-diffusion equations are among the most widely used differential equations in applications. These equations govern the evolution (in time) of species concentrations at various spatial locations that are simultaneously diffusing and undergoing chemical reactions. We consider a reaction-diffusion system that concerns the three species 𝒳1,𝒳2\mathcal{X}_{1},\mathcal{X}_{2} and 𝒳3\mathcal{X}_{3} involved in the following reversible reaction:

𝒳1+𝒳2<>[]​[]​𝒳3\mathrm{$\mathcal{X}_{1}$+$\mathcal{X}_{2}$<>[][]$\mathcal{X}_{3}$}

The spatial domain is taken to be a bounded domain Ω⊂ℝN\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{N} with C2+ν\mathrm{C}^{2+\nu} boundary with ν>0\nu>0. For the unknowns a,b,c:[0,T)×Ω→ℝa,b,c:[0,T)\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}, representing the concentrations of the three species 𝒳1,𝒳2,𝒳3\mathcal{X}_{1},\mathcal{X}_{2},\mathcal{X}_{3} respectively, we consider the following system of differential equations:

(1) {∂ta−da​Δ​a=c−ab in (0,T)×Ω,∂tb−db​Δ​b=c−ab in (0,T)×Ω,∂tc−dc​Δ​c=ab−c in (0,T)×Ω,∇xa⋅n=∇xb⋅n=∇xc⋅n=0 on (0,T)×∂Ω,a(0,⋅)=a0;b(0,⋅)=b0;c⁡(0,⋅)=c0 in ​Ω.\left\{\begin{aligned} \partial_{t}a-d_{a}\Delta a&=c-ab\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \partial_{t}b-d_{b}\Delta b&=c-ab\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \partial_{t}c-d_{c}\Delta c&=ab-c\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \nabla_{x}a\cdot n=\nabla_{x}b\cdot n&=\nabla_{x}c\cdot n=0\quad\mbox{ on }(0,T)\times\partial\Omega,\\ a(0,\cdot)=a_{0};\,b(0,\cdot)=b_{0};\,&c(0,\cdot)=c_{0}\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }\Omega.\end{aligned}\right.

Here n⁡(x)n(x) denotes the outward unit normal to Ω\Omega at the point x∈∂Ωx\in\partial\Omega. The initial data a0,b0,c0a_{0},b_{0},c_{0} are taken to be smooth up to the closure of the domain and strictly positive. The diffusion coefficients da,db,dcd_{a},d_{b},d_{c} are taken to be nonnegative. When all the diffusion coefficients are strictly positive (referred to, now onwards, as the non-degenerate setting), it is well-known that a unique strictly positive global-in-time C∞\mathrm{C}^{\infty} solution exists for the above model (see [11, 12]), where the positiveness comes from the quasi-positive nature of the rate function [14, 1, 13]. The long time behaviour of solutions to (1) in the non-degenerate setting was addressed in [4] using the method of entropy. In this method, a Lyapunov functional (termed entropy) is found for the evolution equation. The negative of the time derivative of this entropy functional is referred to as the entropy dissipation functional. The entropy dissipation functional is then related back to the relative entropy via a functional inequality. This will then be followed by a Grönwall type argument to deduce convergence of relative entropy to zero. A Cziszár-Kullback-Pinsker type inequality that relates relative entropy and the L1\mathrm{L}^{1}-norm helps the authors in [4] to prove the convergence to equilibrium in the L1​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)-norm and to deduce that the decay is exponentially fast in time. In the proof of [4], uniform boundedness of the solution (a,b,c)(a,b,c) to (1) plays an important role. This uniform bound is available in the non-degenerate case.

In this paper, we discuss the long time behaviour of solutions to a couple of degenerate cases of the three species model (1). Our work is heavily inspired by [7] which dealt with a four species degenerate model where one of the species stops diffusing. The authors in [7] demonstrated a so-called indirect diffusion effect wherein an effective diffusion is felt by the non-diffusive species, thanks to the interplay between the diffusion from diffusive species and the underlying reversible reaction. Our work demonstrates that a similar indirect diffusion effect is present in the above three species model in the presence of degeneracies. The two degenerate reaction-diffusion systems that we study in this article are:

(2) {∂ta−da​Δ​a=c−ab in (0,T)×Ω,∂tb=c−ab in (0,T)×Ω,∂tc−dc​Δ​c=ab−c in (0,T)×Ω,∇xa⋅n=∇xb⋅n=∇xc⋅n=0 on (0,T)×∂Ω,a(0,⋅)=a0;b(0,⋅)=b0;c⁡(0,⋅)=c0 in ​Ω,\left\{\begin{aligned} \partial_{t}a-d_{a}\Delta a&=c-ab\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \partial_{t}b&=c-ab\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \partial_{t}c-d_{c}\Delta c&=ab-c\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \nabla_{x}a\cdot n=\nabla_{x}b\cdot n&=\nabla_{x}c\cdot n=0\quad\mbox{ on }(0,T)\times\partial\Omega,\\ a(0,\cdot)=a_{0};\,b(0,\cdot)=b_{0};\,&c(0,\cdot)=c_{0}\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }\Omega,\end{aligned}\right.

and

(3) {∂ta−da​Δ​a=c−ab in (0,T)×Ω,∂tb−db​Δ​b=c−ab in (0,T)×Ω,∂tc=ab−c in (0,T)×Ω,∇xa⋅n=∇xb⋅n=∇xc⋅n=0 on (0,T)×∂Ω,a(0,⋅)=a0;b(0,⋅)=b0;c⁡(0,⋅)=c0 in ​Ω.\left\{\begin{aligned} \partial_{t}a-d_{a}\Delta a&=c-ab\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \partial_{t}b-d_{b}\Delta b&=c-ab\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \partial_{t}c&=ab-c\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }(0,T)\times\Omega,\\ \nabla_{x}a\cdot n=\nabla_{x}b\cdot n&=\nabla_{x}c\cdot n=0\quad\mbox{ on }(0,T)\times\partial\Omega,\\ a(0,\cdot)=a_{0};\,b(0,\cdot)=b_{0};\,&c(0,\cdot)=c_{0}\qquad\qquad\mbox{ in }\Omega.\end{aligned}\right.

Here, the initial data are assumed to be smooth and strictly positive. The diffusion coefficients da,dcd_{a},d_{c} in (2) and the diffusion coefficients da,dbd_{a},d_{b} in (3) are assumed to be strictly positive. The existence of a smooth global-in-time positive solution to (2) was proved in [5, Theorem 3.1]. The existence of a smooth global-in-time positive solution to (3) was proved in [5, Theorem 3.2] if the dimension N≤3N\leq 3. The authors in [5], however, prove the existence of a weak global-in-time positive solution to (3) in any arbitrary dimension.

The process of establishing various estimates in [7] has greatly motivated us to establish similar kind of estimates in dimension larger than three for the degenerate case (2) corresponding to the vanishing of the diffusion coefficient dbd_{b}. We further use various Neumann Green’s function results from [14, 10, 3, 8] to get various estimates specifically for dimensions less than four.

Observe that both the models (2) and (3) satisfy the following mass conservation properties:

(4) 0<M1|Ω|=:∫Ω(a⁡(t,x)+c⁡(t,x))​𝑑x=∫Ω(a⁡(0,x)+c⁡(0,x))​𝑑x,\displaystyle 0<M_{1}|\Omega|=:\int_{\Omega}\big(a(t,x)+c(t,x)\big)\,{\rm d}x=\int_{\Omega}\big(a(0,x)+c(0,x)\big)\,{\rm d}x,
(5) 0<M2|Ω|=:∫Ω(b⁡(t,x)+c⁡(t,x))​𝑑x=∫Ω(b⁡(0,x)+c⁡(0,x))​𝑑x.\displaystyle 0<M_{2}|\Omega|=:\int_{\Omega}\big(b(t,x)+c(t,x)\big)\,{\rm d}x=\int_{\Omega}\big(b(0,x)+c(0,x)\big)\,{\rm d}x.

An homogenous (constant) equilibrium state (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) associated with these models should also satisfy the above conservation properties. Hence we should have

(6) a∞+c∞=M1,b∞+c∞=M2.\displaystyle a_{\infty}+c_{\infty}=M_{1},\qquad b_{\infty}+c_{\infty}=M_{2}.

Moreover, at equilibrium, the rate function should vanish, i.e.

(7) c∞=a∞​b∞.\displaystyle c_{\infty}=a_{\infty}b_{\infty}.

The relations (6) and (7) put together leads to a quadratic equation for c∞c_{\infty} whose only admissible non-negative solution is

(8) c∞=12​(1+M1+M2)−12​(1+M1+M2)2−4​M1​M2.\displaystyle c_{\infty}=\frac{1}{2}(1+M_{1}+M_{2})-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(1+M_{1}+M_{2})^{2}-4M_{1}M_{2}}.

The corresponding a∞a_{\infty} and b∞b_{\infty} can be computed using (6). Now onwards, we will be considering this unique homogeneous equilibrium state (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}). We consider the following entropy functional associated with (2) and (3):

(9) E⁡(a,b,c):=∫Ω((a⁡(ln⁡a−1)+1)+(b⁡(ln⁡b−1)+1)+(c⁡(ln⁡c−1)+1))​𝑑x.\displaystyle E(a,b,c):=\int_{\Omega}\Big((a(\ln a-1)+1)+(b(\ln b-1)+1)+(c(\ln c-1)+1)\Big){\rm d}x.

While studying (2) in dimensions N≥4N\geq 4, we have been able to arrive at large time asymptotics of the solution only under certain closeness assumption on the non-zero diffusion coefficients. The precise assumption is the following:

Assumption 1.

The non-zero diffusion coefficients dad_{a} and dcd_{c} are said to satisfy the closeness assumption if

(10) |da−dc|<2Cda+dc2,p′P​R​C and |da−dc|da+dc<1CS​O​R​(Ω,N,p′),\displaystyle|{d_{a}-d_{c}}|<\frac{2}{C^{PRC}_{{\frac{d_{a}+d_{c}}{2}},p^{\prime}}}\qquad\text{ and }\qquad\frac{|d_{a}-d_{c}|}{d_{a}+d_{c}}<\frac{1}{C_{SOR}(\Omega,N,p^{\prime})},

where the constants Cda+dc2,p′P​R​CC^{PRC}_{{\frac{d_{a}+d_{c}}{2}},p^{\prime}} and CS​O​R​(Ω,N,p′)C_{SOR}(\Omega,N,p^{\prime}), are the parabolic regularity constant (see Theorem 12 in the Appendix) and the second order regularity constant (see Theorem 11 in the Appendix), respectively.

Now we are going to state our two main results.

Theorem 1.

For N≥4N\geq 4, let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (2). Let (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) be the associated equilibrium state given by (6)-(8). Let the nonzero diffusion coefficients da,dcd_{a},d_{c} satisfy the closeness condition (10). Then, for any given positive ε≪1\varepsilon\ll 1, there exists a time TεT_{\varepsilon} and two positive constants 𝒮1\mathcal{S}_{1} and 𝒮2\mathcal{S}_{2} such that for t≥Tεt\geq T_{\varepsilon}, we have

12​M1​‖a−a∞‖L1​(Ω)2+12​M2​‖b−b∞‖L1​(Ω)2+1(M1+M2)​‖c−c∞‖L1​(Ω)2≤(9+2​2)(3+2​2)​|Ω|​𝒮1​e−𝒮2​(1+t)1−ϵN−1.\frac{1}{2M_{1}}\|a-a_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{1}{2M_{2}}\|b-b_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{1}{(M_{1}+M_{2})}\|c-c_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq\frac{(9+2\sqrt{2})}{(3+2\sqrt{2})|\Omega|}\mathcal{S}_{1}e^{-\mathcal{S}_{2}(1+t)^{\frac{1-\epsilon}{N-1}}}.

For N<4N<4, let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (2). Let (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) be the associated equilibrium state given by (6)-(8). Then, for any given positive ε≪1\varepsilon\ll 1, there exists a time TεT_{\varepsilon} and two positive constants 𝒮3\mathcal{S}_{3} and 𝒮4\mathcal{S}_{4} such that for t≥Tεt\geq T_{\varepsilon}, we have

12​M1​‖a−a∞‖L1​(Ω)2+12​M2​‖b−b∞‖L1​(Ω)2+1(M1+M2)​‖c−c∞‖L1​(Ω)2≤(9+2​2)(3+2​2)​|Ω|​𝒮3​e−𝒮4​(1+t)1−ϵ6.\frac{1}{2M_{1}}\|a-a_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{1}{2M_{2}}\|b-b_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{1}{(M_{1}+M_{2})}\|c-c_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq\frac{(9+2\sqrt{2})}{(3+2\sqrt{2})|\Omega|}\mathcal{S}_{3}\,e^{-\mathcal{S}_{4}(1+t)^{\frac{1-\epsilon}{6}}}.

Observe that our above result is unconditional when the dimension N≤3N\leq 3, i.e. there is no closeness assumption on the non-zero diffusion coefficients dad_{a} and dcd_{c}. Furthermore, the constants M1M_{1} and M2M_{2} are determined by the initial data (see (4) and (5)).

Theorem 2.

Let N≤3N\leq 3 and let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (3). Let (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) be the associated equilibrium state given by (6)-(8). Then, for any given positive ε≪1\varepsilon\ll 1, there exists a time TεT_{\varepsilon} and two positive constants 𝒮5\mathcal{S}_{5} and 𝒮6\mathcal{S}_{6} such that for t≥Tεt\geq T_{\varepsilon}, we have

12​M1​‖a−a∞‖L1​(Ω)2+12​M2​‖b−b∞‖L1​(Ω)2+1(M1+M2)​‖c−c∞‖L1​(Ω)2≤(9+2​2)(3+2​2)​|Ω|​𝒮5​e−𝒮6​(1+t)2−ϵ3.\frac{1}{2M_{1}}\|a-a_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{1}{2M_{2}}\|b-b_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}+\frac{1}{(M_{1}+M_{2})}\|c-c_{\infty}\|_{L^{1}(\Omega)}^{2}\leq\frac{(9+2\sqrt{2})}{(3+2\sqrt{2})|\Omega|}\mathcal{S}_{5}\,e^{-\mathcal{S}_{6}(1+t)^{\frac{2-\epsilon}{3}}}.

In the reminder of this introduction, we briefly describe our strategy to arrive at the aforementioned large time behaviour via the entropy method. We start by defining the entropy dissipation functionals associated with the degenerate models (2) and (3):

(11) {For​db=0,D⁡(a,b,c):= 4​da​∫Ω|∇a|2​dx+ 4​dc​∫Ω|∇c|2​dx+∫Ω(a​b−c)​ln⁡(a​bc)​dx,For​dc=0,D⁡(a,b,c):= 4​da​∫Ω|∇a|2​dx+ 4​db​∫Ω|∇b|2​dx+∫Ω(a​b−c)​ln⁡(a​bc)​dx.\left\{\begin{aligned} \text{For}\ d_{b}&=0,\\ D(a,b,c):=&\,4\,d_{a}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla\sqrt{a}\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\,4\,d_{c}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla\sqrt{c}\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\int_{\Omega}(ab-c)\ln\left(\frac{ab}{c}\right)\,{\rm d}x,\\ \text{For}\ d_{c}&=0,\\ D(a,b,c):=&\,4\,d_{a}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla\sqrt{a}\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\,4\,d_{b}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla\sqrt{b}\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\int_{\Omega}(ab-c)\ln\left(\frac{ab}{c}\right)\,{\rm d}x.\end{aligned}\right.

Note that both the dissipation functionals are positive. We recall here an algebraic inequality:

(x−y)​(ln⁡x−ln⁡y)≥4​(x−y)2,∀x,y≥0.(x-y)(\ln{x}-\ln{y})\geq 4(\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{y})^{2},\ \ \forall x,y\geq 0.

This algebraic inequality gives a lower bound on the last term of the above entropy dissipation functionals whereas the classical Poincaré inequality gives a lower bound for the gradient terms. More precisely, we have

(12) {D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L2​(Ω)2+4​dcP⁡(Ω)​‖δC‖L2​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2, for ​db=0,D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L2​(Ω)2+4​dbP⁡(Ω)​‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2, for ​dc=0,\left\{\begin{aligned} D(a,b,c)\geq&\frac{4\,d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{A}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+\frac{4\,d_{c}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+4\|AB-C\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)},\qquad\mbox{ for }\,d_{b}=0,\\ D(a,b,c)\geq&\frac{4\,d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{A}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+\frac{4\,d_{b}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{B}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+4\|AB-C\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)},\qquad\mbox{ for }\,d_{c}=0,\\ \end{aligned}\right.

where P⁡(Ω)P(\Omega) is the Poincaré constant of the domain Ω\Omega (see Lemma 7 in the Appendix). Observe that the deviation term ‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2\|\delta_{B}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} is missing in the above lower bound corresponding to the degenerate case db=0d_{b}=0 and the deviation term ‖δC‖L2​(Ω)2\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} is missing in the lower bound corresponding to the degenerate case dc=0d_{c}=0. Note that, for the dissipation functional of the degenerate system (2), the Poincaré inequality actually yields

{D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L2​NN−2​(Ω)2+4​dcP⁡(Ω)​‖δC‖L2​NN−2​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2 for ​N≥4,D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L6​(Ω)2+4​dcP⁡(Ω)​‖δC‖L6​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2 for ​N≤3.\left\{\begin{aligned} D(a,b,c)\geq&\frac{4\,d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{A}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{2N}{N-2}}(\Omega)}+\frac{4\,d_{c}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{2N}{N-2}}(\Omega)}+4\|AB-C\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,N\geq 4,\\ D(a,b,c)\geq&\frac{4\,d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{A}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+\frac{4\,d_{c}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+4\|AB-C\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\qquad\qquad\quad\mbox{ for }N\leq 3.\end{aligned}\right.

{D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L2​NN−2​(Ω)2+4​dbP⁡(Ω)​‖δB‖L2​NN−2​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2 for ​N≥4,D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L6​(Ω)2+4​dbP⁡(Ω)​‖δB‖L6​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2 for ​N≤3.\left\{\begin{aligned} D(a,b,c)\geq&\frac{4\,d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{A}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{2N}{N-2}}(\Omega)}+\frac{4\,d_{b}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{B}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{2N}{N-2}}(\Omega)}+4\|AB-C\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\qquad\mbox{ for }N\geq 4,\\ D(a,b,c)\geq&\frac{4\,d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{A}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+\frac{4\,d_{b}}{P(\Omega)}\|\delta_{B}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+4\|AB-C\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\qquad\qquad\quad\mbox{ for }N\leq 3.\end{aligned}\right.

Note that, if (a,b,c)(a,b,c) solves either of the system (2) or (3), we have

(13) E(a,b,c)−E(a∞,b∞,c∞)=∫Ω(aln(aa∞)−a+a∞)dx+∫Ω\displaystyle E(a,b,c)-E(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty})=\int_{\Omega}\left(a\ln{\left(\frac{a}{a_{\infty}}\right)}-a+a_{\infty}\right)\,{\rm d}x+\int_{\Omega} (b​ln⁡(bb∞)−b+b∞)​d​x\displaystyle\left(b\ln{\left(\frac{b}{b_{\infty}}\right)}-b+b_{\infty}\right)\,{\rm d}x
+∫Ω(cln(cc∞)−c+c∞)dx.\displaystyle+\int_{\Omega}\left(c\ln{\left(\frac{c}{c_{\infty}}\right)}-c+c_{\infty}\right)\,{\rm d}x.

Define a function Γ:(0,∞)×(0,∞)→ℝ\Gamma:(0,\infty)\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R} as follows:

Observe that, other than the logarithm of the growth of the supremum norm of the solution, the growth of relative entropy depends on the L2​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega) norm of the deviation of the (A,B,C)(A,B,C) from (A∞,B∞,C∞)(A_{\infty},B_{\infty},C_{\infty}). This indicates that to relate entropy with entropy dissipation, we need to relate dissipation with the missing term ‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2\|\delta_{B}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} for the degenerate case (2) and similarly with the missing term ‖δC‖L2​(Ω)2\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} for the degenerate case (3).

For the degenerate system (2), the relation between the missing term and the entropy dissipation is shown in Proposition 4 for dimensions N≥4N\geq 4. For dimensions N≤3N\leq 3, we obtain the relation in Proposition 5. More precisely, we have obtained

{D⁡(a,b,c)≥C^​(1+t)−N−2N−1​‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2 for ​N≥4,D⁡(a,b,c)≥C^​(1+t)−56​‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2 for ​N≤3.\left\{\begin{aligned} D(a,b,c)\geq&\,\hat{C}(1+t)^{-\frac{N-2}{N-1}}\|\delta_{B}\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\qquad\mbox{ for }N\geq 4,\\ D(a,b,c)\geq&\,\hat{C}(1+t)^{-\frac{5}{6}}\|\delta_{B}\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\qquad\quad\mbox{ for }N\leq 3.\end{aligned}\right.

where C^\hat{C} is some positive constant, independent of time.

In order to obtain the above lower bound, we require an estimate on the growth (in time) of the LN2​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{\frac{N}{2}}(\Omega) norm of the degenerate species bb for dimension N≥4N\geq 4 and for dimension N≤3N\leq 3, we require a similar growth estimate of the L32​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega) norm of the degenerate species bb. These estimates are obtained in Lemma 2, Proposition 3 and Lemma 3. More precisely, we have obtained

{‖b‖LN2​(Ω)≤K^(1+t)N−2N−1N≥4,‖b‖L32​(Ω)≤K^(1+t)56N=1,2,3,\left\{\begin{aligned} \|b\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{N}{2}}(\Omega)}&\leq\hat{K}(1+t)^{\frac{N-2}{N-1}}\qquad N\geq 4,\\ \|b\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)}&\leq\hat{K}(1+t)^{\frac{5}{6}}\qquad N=1,2,3,\end{aligned}\right.

where K^\hat{K} is a positive constant independent of time. For dimension N≤3N\leq 3, the above integral estimation of the species bb follows from Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality whereas for dimension N≥4N\geq 4, we need closeness assumption (10) on the other two non-zero diffusion coefficients dad_{a} and dcd_{c}. Closeness assumption further helps us to estimate Lp\mathrm{L}^{p} integral growth of aa and cc on a parabolic cylinder with unit height, for some large exponent pp. It turns out if dad_{a} and dcd_{c} satisfy the closeness condition (10) for dimension N≥4N\geq 4, then there exists a positive constant C0>0C_{0}>0, depending on pp and independent of time, such that

‖a‖Lp​((τ,τ+1)×Ω)+‖c‖Lp​((τ,τ+1)×Ω)≤C0∀τ≥0,p>N.\|a\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}((\tau,\tau+1)\times\Omega)}+\|c\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}((\tau,\tau+1)\times\Omega)}\leq C_{0}\qquad\forall\tau\geq 0,\ p>N.

The above result is proved in Lemma 1. For dimension N≥4N\geq 4, this will lead us to prove our key LN2​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{\frac{N}{2}}(\Omega) estimate. These strategies are inspired from the article [7], where the authors study existence and large time behaviour of a particular 4×44\times 4 quadratic degenerate reaction-diffusion system.

For the degenerate system (3), we will relate the entropy dissipation functional with the missing term ‖δC‖L2​(Ω)2\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}. In this article, for the degenerate case (3), we analyze the decay of entropy in dimension N≤3N\leq 3. We will establish our result only for dimension N=3N=3. For dimension N=1,2N=1,2, all the calculations are similar. In Proposition 9 We establish the following relation between the entropy dissipation and the missing term ‖δC‖L2​(Ω)2\|\delta_{C}\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}

D⁡(a,b,c)≥C^​(1+t)−13​(‖A−A¯‖L2​(Ω)2+‖B−B¯‖L2​(Ω)2+‖C−C¯‖L2​(Ω)2).D(a,b,c)\geq\hat{C}(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{3}}\left(\|A-\overline{A}\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}+\|B-\overline{B}\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}+\|C-\overline{C}\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}\right).

‖a‖L32​(Ω)≤C~​(1+t)13∀t≥0\|a\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq\tilde{C}(1+t)^{\frac{1}{3}}\qquad\forall t\geq 0

These results, along with the Grönwall inequality, will lead us to the conclusion that the entropy functional decays sub-exponentially fast in time for both the degenerate systems (2) and (3). On the other hand, an application of the Cziszár-Kullback-Pinsker inequality yields the following lower bound on the relative entropy (see [4] for details):

Combining all these estimates we arrive at our main results: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2.

A similar estimate was obtained for a degenerate four species model in [7, Lemma 3.12, p.4343].

The following lemma derives the key integrability estimate for the concentration bb which will play an important role in our analysis.

Lemma 2.

Let p>N≥4p>N\geq 4 and let p′p^{\prime} be its Hölder conjugate. Let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenrate system (2) and let the nonzero diffusion coefficients da,dcd_{a},d_{c} satisfy the closeness condition (10). Then there exists a constant K3>0K_{3}>0, depending only on the initial data and the dimension N, such that

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN2​(Ω)≤K3​(1+t)N−2N−1∀t≥0.\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{N}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq K_{3}\,(1+t)^{\frac{N-2}{N-1}}\qquad\forall t\geq 0.
Proof.

Recall that bb solves the equation

∂tb=c−a​b.\partial_{t}b=c-ab.

Non-negativity of aa and bb implies that

∂tb≤c.\partial_{t}b\leq c.

Integrating over (0,t)(0,t) yields

b⁡(t,x)≤b0​(x)+∫0tc⁡(s,x)​𝑑s.b(t,x)\leq b_{0}(x)+\int_{0}^{t}c(s,x)\,{\rm d}s.

Raising it to the power NN and employing Jensen’s inequality, we obtain

(b⁡(t,x))N≤2N−1​((b0​(x))N+(∫0tc⁡(s,x)​𝑑s)N)≤2N−1​(1+t)N−1​((b0​(x))N+∫0t(c⁡(s,x))N​𝑑s).\left(b(t,x)\right)^{N}\leq 2^{N-1}\left(\left(b_{0}(x)\right)^{N}+\left(\int_{0}^{t}c(s,x)\,{\rm d}s\right)^{N}\right)\leq 2^{N-1}(1+t)^{N-1}\left(\left(b_{0}(x)\right)^{N}+\int_{0}^{t}\left(c(s,x)\right)^{N}\,{\rm d}s\right).

Integrating the above inequality in the xx variable over Ω\Omega yields

(26) ‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN​(Ω)N≤2N−1​(1+t)N−1​(‖b0‖LN​(Ω)N+‖c‖LN​(Ωt)N).\displaystyle\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega)}^{N}\leq 2^{N-1}(1+t)^{N-1}\Big(\left\|b_{0}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega)}^{N}+\left\|c\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega_{t})}^{N}\Big).

According to Lemma 1, for any p>Np>N and for any τ≥0\tau\geq 0, we have

‖c‖Lp​(Ωτ,τ+1)≤C0,\left\|c\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}(\Omega_{\tau,\tau+1})}\leq C_{0},

where the constant C0>0C_{0}>0 depends only on the dimension NN, the domain Ω\Omega and the initial data. Hölder inequality yields

‖c‖LN​(Ωτ,τ+1)≤‖c‖Lp​(Ωτ,τ+1)​|Ω|p−Np.\left\|c\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega_{\tau,\tau+1})}\leq\left\|c\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}(\Omega_{\tau,\tau+1})}\,\left|\Omega\right|^{\frac{p-N}{p}}.

Hence we deduce that for any t>0t>0,

‖c‖LN​(Ωt)N≤C0N​|Ω|N⁡(p−N)p​(1+t).\left\|c\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega_{t})}^{N}\leq C_{0}^{N}\,\left|\Omega\right|^{\frac{N(p-N)}{p}}\,(1+t).

Using this in (26) yields

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN​(Ω)N≤2N−1​(1+t)N−1​(‖b0‖L∞​(Ω)N​|Ω|+C0N​|Ω|N⁡(p−N)p​(1+t)).\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega)}^{N}\leq 2^{N-1}(1+t)^{N-1}\left(\left\|b_{0}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega)}^{N}\,\left|\Omega\right|+C_{0}^{N}\,\left|\Omega\right|^{\frac{N(p-N)}{p}}\,(1+t)\right).

Define a constant K3>0K_{3}>0 as follows:

K3N⁡(N−1)N−2:=2N−1​(M2​|Ω|)NN−2​(‖b0‖L∞​(Ω)N​|Ω|+C0N​|Ω|N⁡(p−N)p).K_{3}^{\frac{N(N-1)}{N-2}}:=2^{N-1}\left(M_{2}|\Omega|\right)^{\frac{N}{N-2}}\left(\left\|b_{0}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega)}^{N}\,\left|\Omega\right|+C_{0}^{N}\,\left|\Omega\right|^{\frac{N(p-N)}{p}}\right).

Thus we arrive at

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN​(Ω)≤K3N−1N−2​(M2​|Ω|)−1N−2​(1+t).\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega)}\leq K_{3}^{\frac{N-1}{N-2}}\left(M_{2}|\Omega|\right)^{-\frac{1}{N-2}}(1+t).

Note that

2N=αN+1−α1 with ​α=N−2N−1.\frac{2}{N}=\frac{\alpha}{N}+\frac{1-\alpha}{1}\qquad\mbox{ with }\,\alpha=\frac{N-2}{N-1}.

Hence by interpolation, we have

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN2​(Ω)≤‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN​(Ω)N−2N−1​‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖L1​(Ω)1N−1.\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{N}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{N}(\Omega)}^{\frac{N-2}{N-1}}\,\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}^{\frac{1}{N-1}}.

This yields the following estimate:

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖LN2​(Ω)≤K3​(1+t)N−2N−1.\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{N}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq K_{3}\,(1+t)^{\frac{N-2}{N-1}}.

Unlike the case of dimension N≥4N\geq 4, we are able to obtain L32​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)-norm estimates on b⁡(t,⋅)b(t,\cdot) without any closeness assumption on the diffusion coefficients dad_{a} and dcd_{c} in the case of dimensions N≤3N\leq 3. Next, we prove such an estimate and more in dimension three followed by a similar result in dimensions one and two.

Proposition 3.

Let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (2) in dimension N=3N=3. Then, there exist constants K^,Kc>0\hat{K},K_{c}>0 and μc∈ℕ\mu_{c}\in\mathbb{N}, independent of time, such that

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖L32​(Ω)\displaystyle\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)} ≤K^​(1+t)56 for ​t≥0,\displaystyle\leq\hat{K}(1+t)^{\frac{5}{6}}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,t\geq 0,
‖a‖L72​(Ωτ,τ+1)\displaystyle\left\|a\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{7}{2}}(\Omega_{\tau,\tau+1})} ≤Kc for ​τ≥0,\displaystyle\leq K_{c}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,\tau\geq 0,

A result similar to that of Proposition 6 can be found when the dimension N<4N<4. The proof goes along similar lines and we skip it in the interest of space. The proof banks on the lower bound for the dissipation functional obtained in Proposition 5. The key point to be noted, however, is that this result is unconditional in the sense that the nonzero diffusion coefficients are not assumed to satisfy the closeness condition (10).

Proposition 7.

Let N<4N<4 and let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (2). Let (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) be the associated equilibrium state given by (6)-(8). We are now equipped to prove our main result of this section.

Proof of Theorem 1:

We have already obtained sub-exponential decay (in time) of the relative entropy in Proposition 6 (for dimension N≥4N\geq 4) and in Proposition 7 (for dimension N<4N<4). Hence the sub-exponential decay in the L1\mathrm{L}^{1}-norm is a direct consequence of the following Cziszár-Kullback-Pinsker type inequality that relates relative entropy and the L1\mathrm{L}^{1}-norm:

E⁡(a,b,c)−E⁡(a∞,b∞,c∞)≥(3+2​2)​|Ω|2​M1​(9+2​2)\displaystyle E(a,b,c)-E(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty})\geq\frac{\left(3+2\sqrt{2}\right)|\Omega|}{2M_{1}\left(9+2\sqrt{2}\right)} ‖a−a∞‖L1​(Ω)2+(3+2​2)​|Ω|2​M1​(9+2​2)​‖b−b∞‖L1​(Ω)2\displaystyle\left\|a-a_{\infty}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}+\frac{\left(3+2\sqrt{2}\right)|\Omega|}{2M_{1}\left(9+2\sqrt{2}\right)}\left\|b-b_{\infty}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}
+(3+2​2)​|Ω|(M1+M2)​(9+2​2)​‖c−c∞‖L1​(Ω)2.\displaystyle+\frac{\left(3+2\sqrt{2}\right)|\Omega|}{\left(M_{1}+M_{2}\right)\left(9+2\sqrt{2}\right)}\left\|c-c_{\infty}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}.

The proof of the above functional inequality is available in [4, Lemma 3.3, p.173] which exploits the conservation properties (4) and (5). ∎

3. The case of dc=0d_{c}=0

In this section, we shall devote our attention to the study of the degenerate model (3) which corresponds to the vanishing of the diffusion coefficient dcd_{c}. The existence of a smooth positive solution to (3) was proved in [5, Theorem 3.2] for all smooth initial non-negative data if the dimension N≤3N\leq 3. Our main objective of this section is to understand the large time behaviour of solutions to (3). Here, we choose to present our computations when the dimension N=3N=3. Analogous results hold true in dimensions one and two as well. Note that we have the entropy equality

dd​t​(E⁡(a,b,c)−E⁡(a∞,b∞,c∞))=−D⁡(a,b,c) for all ​t>0,\frac{{\rm d}}{{\rm d}t}\left(E(a,b,c)-E(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty})\right)=-D(a,b,c)\qquad\mbox{ for all }t>0,

where (a,b,c)(a,b,c) is the solution to the degenerate model (3) and (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) is the corresponding equilibrium state given by (6) and (8). The dissipation functional DD in the above equality is given by

D⁡(a,b,c)=4​da​∫Ω|∇A|2​𝑑x+4​db​∫Ω|∇B|2​𝑑x+∫Ω(a​b−c)​ln⁡(a​bc)​𝑑x.D(a,b,c)=4d_{a}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla A\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+4d_{b}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla B\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\int_{\Omega}(ab-c)\ln\left(\frac{ab}{c}\right)\,{\rm d}x.

We arrive at the following straightforward lower bound for the dissipation:

(57) D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​daP⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L6​(Ω)2+4​dbP⁡(Ω)​‖δB‖L6​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2,\displaystyle D(a,b,c)\geq\frac{4d_{a}}{P(\Omega)}\left\|\delta_{A}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+\frac{4d_{b}}{P(\Omega)}\left\|\delta_{B}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+4\left\|AB-C\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)},

thanks to the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality and an algebraic identity which says that for all p,q≥0p,q\geq 0, there holds (p−q)​(ln⁡p−ln⁡q)≥4​(p−q)2(p-q)\left(\ln p-\ln q\right)\geq 4\left(\sqrt{p}-\sqrt{q}\right)^{2}. An application of the Hölder inequality leads to

(58) D⁡(a,b,c)≥4​da​|Ω|−23P⁡(Ω)​‖δA‖L2​(Ω)2+4​db​|Ω|−23P⁡(Ω)​‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2+4​‖A​B−C‖L2​(Ω)2.\displaystyle D(a,b,c)\geq\frac{4d_{a}\left|\Omega\right|^{-\frac{2}{3}}}{P(\Omega)}\left\|\delta_{A}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+\frac{4d_{b}\left|\Omega\right|^{-\frac{2}{3}}}{P(\Omega)}\left\|\delta_{B}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+4\left\|AB-C\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}.

It is apparent from the above inequality that the term involving ‖δC‖L2​(Ω)2\left\|\delta_{C}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} is missing from its lower bound. A similar scenario was handled in the previous section while dealing with the missing ‖δB‖L2​(Ω)2\left\|\delta_{B}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} term. Our strategy was to derive polynomial (in time) bounds on the supremum norms of the concentrations. Here too, we will adapt a similar approach. Note, however, that the proofs of most results in this section markedly differ from the proofs in the previous section. We begin with a time-dependent L1​(Ω)\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega) estimate on certain combinations of the concentrations. This result is inspired by [6, Theorem 3.1, p.495]. Our proof argues along similar lines as in [6] while keeping track of the polynomial (in time) bound.

Lemma 5.

Let N≤3N\leq 3 and let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (3). Then, there exist positive constants ℓ1\ell_{1} and ℓ2\ell_{2} such that for all t≥0t\geq 0, we have

∫0t∫Ω(a2​(s,x)+a⁡(s,x)​c​(s,x))​𝑑x​𝑑s\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Omega}\Big(a^{2}(s,x)+a(s,x)c(s,x)\Big)\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}s ≤ℓ1​(1+t),\displaystyle\leq\ell_{1}\left(1+t\right),
∫0t∫Ω(b2​(s,x)+b⁡(s,x)​c​(s,x))​𝑑x​𝑑s\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Omega}\Big(b^{2}(s,x)+b(s,x)c(s,x)\Big)\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}s ≤ℓ2​(1+t).\displaystyle\leq\ell_{2}\left(1+t\right).
Proof.

Adding up the equations for aa and cc in the degenerate model (3), we obtain

(59) ∂t(a+c)−da​Δ​a=0.\displaystyle\partial_{t}\left(a+c\right)-d_{a}\Delta a=0.

Let H∈Cc∞​(Ω)H\in\mathrm{C}^{\infty}_{c}(\Omega) be arbitrary and let Z:=a​daa+cZ:=\frac{a\,d_{a}}{a+c}. Now consider the following backward parabolic problem:

(60) {−∂tw−ZΔw=HZ in ΩT,∇w⋅n⁡(x)=0 on ∂ΩT,w⁡(T,x)=0 in Ω.\left\{\begin{aligned} -\partial_{t}w-Z\Delta w&=H\,\sqrt{Z}\qquad\mbox{ in }\ \Omega_{T},\\ \nabla w\cdot n(x)&=0\qquad\qquad\mbox{ on }\ \partial\Omega_{T},\\ w(T,x)&=0\qquad\qquad\ \mbox{ in }\ \Omega.\end{aligned}\right.

In this duality approach, the idea is to multiply the equation (59) by the solution ww to the backward problem (60) followed by an integration over ΩT\Omega_{T} leading to

thanks to integration by parts. Using the equation satisfied by ww in (60), we deduce the following:

(61) ∫0T∫Ω(a+c)​H​Z​𝑑x​𝑑t=∫Ωw⁡(0,x)​(a0​(x)+c0​(x))​𝑑x≤‖w⁡(0,⋅)‖L2​(Ω)​‖a0+c0‖L2​(Ω),\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\left(a+c\right)\,H\,\sqrt{Z}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t=\int_{\Omega}w(0,x)\left(a_{0}(x)+c_{0}(x)\right)\,{\rm d}x\leq\left\|w(0,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\left\|a_{0}+c_{0}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)},

where the inequality is due to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Our next objective is to get an estimate for ‖w⁡(0,⋅)‖L2​(Ω)\left\|w(0,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}. To that end, multiply the evolution equation by −Δ​w-\Delta w and integrating with respect to the spatial variable yields

∫ΩΔw∂twdx+∫ΩZ(Δw)2dx=−∫ΩHZΔwdx.\int_{\Omega}\Delta w\partial_{t}w\,{\rm d}x+\int_{\Omega}Z\left(\Delta w\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x=-\int_{\Omega}H\sqrt{Z}\Delta w\,{\rm d}x.

Performing an integration by parts in the first term on the left hand side (while using the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition from (60)) and employing Young’s inequality for the term on the right hand side yields

−12dd​t∫Ω|∇w|2dx+∫ΩZ(Δw)2dx≤12∫ΩH2dx+12∫ΩZ(Δw)2dx.-\frac{1}{2}\frac{{\rm d}}{{\rm d}t}\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla w\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\int_{\Omega}Z\left(\Delta w\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x\leq\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}H^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}Z\left(\Delta w\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x.

Integrating the above inequality on the interval (0,T)(0,T) in the time variable results in

(62) ∫Ω|∇w​(0,x)|2​𝑑x+∫0T∫ΩZ​(Δ​w)2​𝑑x​𝑑t≤∫0T∫ΩH2​𝑑x​𝑑t.\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla w(0,x)\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}Z\left(\Delta w\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t\leq\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}H^{2}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t.

∫Ω(w⁡(0,x)−1|Ω|​∫Ωw⁡(0,y)​𝑑y)2​𝑑x≤P⁡(Ω)​∫Ω|∇w​(0,x)|2​𝑑x,\int_{\Omega}\left(w(0,x)-\frac{1}{\left|\Omega\right|}\int_{\Omega}w(0,y)\,{\rm d}y\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x\leq P(\Omega)\int_{\Omega}\left|\nabla w(0,x)\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x,

where P⁡(Ω)P(\Omega) is the Poincaré constant. Note that integrating the evolution equation in (60) over ΩT\Omega_{T} yields

∫Ωw⁡(0,x)​𝑑x\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}w(0,x)\,{\rm d}x =∫0T∫ΩZ​Δ​w​𝑑x​𝑑t+∫0T∫ΩH​Z​𝑑x​𝑑t\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}Z\Delta w\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}H\sqrt{Z}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t
≤((∫0T∫ΩZ​(Δ​w)2​𝑑x​𝑑t)12+(∫0T∫ΩH2​𝑑x​𝑑t)12)​‖Z‖L2​(ΩT)\displaystyle\leq\left(\left(\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}Z\left(\Delta w\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}+\left(\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}H^{2}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\left\|\sqrt{Z}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega_{T})}
≤2​‖H‖L2​(ΩT)​‖Z‖L2​(ΩT)\displaystyle\leq 2\left\|H\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega_{T})}\left\|\sqrt{Z}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega_{T})}

thanks to the estimate from (62). Using the fact that Z≤daZ\leq d_{a}, we deduce

(63) (∫Ωw⁡(0,x)​𝑑x)2≤4​da​T​|Ω|​‖H‖L2​(ΩT)2.\displaystyle\left(\int_{\Omega}w(0,x)\,{\rm d}x\right)^{2}\leq 4d_{a}T\left|\Omega\right|\left\|H\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega_{T})}.

Hence we obtain

∫Ω|w⁡(0,x)|2​𝑑x≤2​∫Ω(w⁡(0,x)−1|Ω|​∫Ωw⁡(0,y)​𝑑y)2​𝑑x+2|Ω|​(∫Ωw⁡(0,x)​𝑑x)2≤(2​P​(Ω)+8​da​T)​‖H‖L2​(ΩT)2,\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}\left|w(0,x)\right|^{2}\,{\rm d}x\leq 2\int_{\Omega}\left(w(0,x)-\frac{1}{\left|\Omega\right|}\int_{\Omega}w(0,y)\,{\rm d}y\right)^{2}\,{\rm d}x+\frac{2}{\left|\Omega\right|}\left(\int_{\Omega}w(0,x)\,{\rm d}x\right)^{2}\leq\left(2P(\Omega)+8d_{a}T\right)\left\|H\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega_{T})},

thanks to (62) and (63). Going back to (61), we have thus obtained

Lemma 6.

Let N≤3N\leq 3 and let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (3). Then, there exist positive constants ℓ3,ℓ4,ℓ7\ell_{3},\ell_{4},\ell_{7} such that

‖a⁡(t,⋅)‖L32​(Ω)\displaystyle\left\|a(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)} ≤ℓ3​(1+t)13 for ​t≥0,\displaystyle\leq\ell_{3}\left(1+t\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,t\geq 0,

‖c⁡(t,⋅)‖L3​(Ω)\displaystyle\left\|c(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{3}(\Omega)} ≤ℓ7​(1+t) for ​t≥0.\displaystyle\leq\ell_{7}\left(1+t\right)\qquad\,\,\mbox{ for }\,t\geq 0.

Multiplying the equation for aa in (3) by aa and integrating in space and time variables yields

where we have used the fact that a,ba,b are non-negative. The estimate from Lemma 5 helps us get

As

131+1−132=23,\frac{\frac{1}{3}}{1}+\frac{1-\frac{1}{3}}{2}=\frac{2}{3},

interpolation leads to the following bound:

‖a⁡(t,⋅)‖L32​(Ω)≤‖a⁡(t,⋅)‖L1​(Ω)13​‖a⁡(t,⋅)‖L2​(Ω)23≤M113​|Ω|13​(‖a0‖L2​(Ω)2+2​ℓ1​(1+t))13\left\|a(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq\left\|a(t,\cdot)\right\|^{\frac{1}{3}}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}\left\|a(t,\cdot)\right\|^{\frac{2}{3}}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\leq M_{1}^{\frac{1}{3}}\left|\Omega\right|^{\frac{1}{3}}\left(\left\|a_{0}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+2\ell_{1}\left(1+t\right)\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}

where we have used the mass conservation property (4). Taking ℓ3:=(M1​|Ω|​(‖a0‖L2​(Ω)2+2​ℓ1))13\ell_{3}:=\left(M_{1}\left|\Omega\right|\left(\left\|a_{0}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+2\ell_{1}\right)\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}, we have thus shown

‖a⁡(t,⋅)‖L32​(Ω)≤ℓ3​(1+t)13 for ​t≥0.\left\|a(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq\ell_{3}\left(1+t\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,t\geq 0.

Arguing exactly as above, we obtain

‖b⁡(t,⋅)‖L32​(Ω)≤ℓ4​(1+t)13 for ​t≥0,\left\|b(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\frac{3}{2}}(\Omega)}\leq\ell_{4}\left(1+t\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,t\geq 0,

with the constant ℓ4=(M2​|Ω|​(‖b0‖L2​(Ω)2+2​ℓ2))13\ell_{4}=\left(M_{2}\left|\Omega\right|\left(\left\|b_{0}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}+2\ell_{2}\right)\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}. It follows from (64) and the estimate from Lemma 5 that

A similar estimate holds for ‖b‖L2​(0,t,H1​(Ω))2\left\|b\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(0,t;\mathrm{H}^{1}(\Omega))} as well. By Sobolev embedding we have

Exploiting the non-negativity of cc, observe from (3) that cc satisfies the inequality ∂tc≤a​b\partial_{t}c\leq ab. Hence we have

(c⁡(t,x))3≤22​((c0​(x))3+(∫0ta⁡(s,x)​b​(s,x)​𝑑s)3)≤22​(1+t)2​((c0​(x))3+∫0t(a⁡(s,x)​b​(s,x))3​𝑑s),\left(c(t,x)\right)^{3}\leq 2^{2}\left(\left(c_{0}(x)\right)^{3}+\left(\int_{0}^{t}a(s,x)\,b(s,x)\,{\rm d}s\right)^{3}\right)\leq 2^{2}(1+t)^{2}\left(\left(c_{0}(x)\right)^{3}+\int_{0}^{t}\left(a(s,x)\,b(s,x)\right)^{3}\,{\rm d}s\right),

Employing the Hölder inequality leads to the following bound

‖c⁡(t,⋅)‖L3​(Ω)3\displaystyle\left\|c(t,\cdot)\right\|^{3}_{\mathrm{L}^{3}(\Omega)} ≤22​(1+t)2​(‖c0‖L3​(Ω)3+∫0t‖a⁡(s,⋅)‖L6​(Ω)12​‖b⁡(s,⋅)‖L6​(Ω)12​𝑑s)\displaystyle\leq 2^{2}(1+t)^{2}\left(\left\|c_{0}\right\|^{3}_{\mathrm{L}^{3}(\Omega)}+\int_{0}^{t}\left\|a(s,\cdot)\right\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}\,\left\|b(s,\cdot)\right\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}\,{\rm d}s\right)
≤22​(1+t)2​(‖c0‖L3​(Ω)3+12​∫0t(‖a⁡(s,⋅)‖L6​(Ω)+‖b⁡(s,⋅)‖L6​(Ω))​𝑑s),\displaystyle\leq 2^{2}(1+t)^{2}\left(\left\|c_{0}\right\|^{3}_{\mathrm{L}^{3}(\Omega)}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{t}\left(\left\|a(s,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}+\left\|b(s,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{6}(\Omega)}\right)\,{\rm d}s\right),

where we have applied the Young’s inequality. Hence it follows from (65) and (66) that

‖c⁡(t,⋅)‖L3​(Ω)≤ℓ7​(1+t) for ​t≥0,\left\|c(t,\cdot)\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{3}(\Omega)}\leq\ell_{7}(1+t)\qquad\mbox{ for }t\geq 0,

for some constant ℓ7\ell_{7} ∎

Our next task is to obtain polynomial (in time) growth estimates on the solution in the supremum norm.

Proposition 8.

Let N≤3N\leq 3 and let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (3). Then, there exist positive constants K∞K_{\infty} and μ\mu such that for all t≥0t\geq 0, we have

‖a‖L∞​(Ωt)\displaystyle\left\|a\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega_{t})} ≤K∞​(1+t)μ\displaystyle\leq K_{\infty}\left(1+t\right)^{\mu}
‖b‖L∞​(Ωt)\displaystyle\left\|b\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega_{t})} ≤K∞​(1+t)μ\displaystyle\leq K_{\infty}\left(1+t\right)^{\mu}
‖c‖L∞​(Ωt)\displaystyle\left\|c\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega_{t})} ≤K∞​(1+t)μ\displaystyle\leq K_{\infty}\left(1+t\right)^{\mu}
Proof.

Let GdaG_{d_{a}} denote the Green’s function associated with the operator ∂t−daΔ\partial_{t}-d_{a}\Delta with Neumann boundary condition. We can express the solution aa as follows:

(67) a⁡(t,x)=a~​(t,x)+∫0t∫ΩGda​(t−s,x,y)​[c−a​b]​(s,y)​𝑑y​𝑑s,\displaystyle a(t,x)=\tilde{a}(t,x)+\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Omega}G_{d_{a}}(t-s,x,y)\left[c-ab\right](s,y)\,{\rm d}y\,{\rm d}s,

where a~\tilde{a} solves the following initial boundary value problem:

{∂ta~−da​Δ​a~=0 in Ωt,∇a~⋅n⁡(x)=0 on ∂Ωt,a~​(0,x)=a0 in Ω.\left\{\begin{aligned} \partial_{t}\tilde{a}-d_{a}\Delta\tilde{a}&=0\qquad\ \mbox{ in }\ \Omega_{t},\\ \nabla\tilde{a}\cdot n(x)&=0\qquad\ \mbox{ on }\ \partial\Omega_{t},\\ \tilde{a}(0,x)&=a_{0}\qquad\mbox{ in }\ \Omega.\end{aligned}\right.

We recall the following Gaussian bound on the Neumann Green’s function (see [10, Theorem 2.2, p.37]): there exist positive constants CH,κ\texttt{C}_{H},\kappa such that

(68) |Gda​(t−s,x,y)|≤CH​1(t−s)N2​e−κ​|x−y|2(t−s)=:g⁡(t−s,x−y)\displaystyle\left|G_{d_{a}}(t-s,x,y)\right|\leq\texttt{C}_{H}\frac{1}{(t-s)^{\frac{N}{2}}}e^{-\kappa\frac{\left|x-y\right|^{2}}{(t-s)}}=:g(t-s,x-y)

Also see [3, Theorem 3.1, p.639] for general parabolic operators. As a consequence we have the following bound on the solution a~\tilde{a} to the above homogeneous problem:

Recall from the lower bound in (58) that the term involving ‖δC‖L2​(Ω)\left\|\delta_{C}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)} is apparently missing. Similar to Propositions 4 and 5, we now derive a lower bound for the dissipation functional involving this missing term.

Thanks to the lower bound in (71), we can derive a sub-exponential decay estimate for the relative entropy.

Proposition 10.

Let N≤3N\leq 3 and let (a,b,c)(a,b,c) be the solution to the degenerate system (3). Let (a∞,b∞,c∞)(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty}) be the associated equilibrium state given by (6)-(8). Then, for any given positive ε≪1\varepsilon\ll 1, there exists a time TεT_{\varepsilon} and two positive constants 𝒮5\mathcal{S}_{5} and 𝒮6\mathcal{S}_{6} such that

(75) E⁡(a,b,c)−E⁡(a∞,b∞,c∞)≤𝒮5​e−𝒮6​(1+t)2−ϵ3 for ​t≥Tε.\displaystyle E(a,b,c)-E(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty})\leq\mathcal{S}_{5}\,e^{-\mathcal{S}_{6}(1+t)^{\frac{2-\epsilon}{3}}}\qquad\mbox{ for }\,t\geq T_{\varepsilon}.

The proof of the above proposition is exactly similar to the proof of Proposition 6. Hence we skip the proof. Note that the constants 𝒮5\mathcal{S}_{5} and 𝒮6\mathcal{S}_{6} appearing in (75) depend on the constant 𝒦c\mathcal{K}_{c} (appearing in Proposition 71), the constants K∞K_{\infty} and μ\mu (appearing in Proposition 8). Finally, we are all equipped to prove our main result of this section.

Proof of Theorem 2.

We have already obtained sub-exponential decay (in time) of the relative entropy (75) in Proposition 10. Hence the sub-exponential decay in the L1\mathrm{L}^{1}-norm is a direct consequence of the following Cziszár-Kullback-Pinsker type inequality that relates relative entropy and the L1\mathrm{L}^{1}-norm:

E⁡(a,b,c)−E⁡(a∞,b∞,c∞)≥(3+2​2)​|Ω|2​M1​(9+2​2)\displaystyle E(a,b,c)-E(a_{\infty},b_{\infty},c_{\infty})\geq\frac{\left(3+2\sqrt{2}\right)|\Omega|}{2M_{1}\left(9+2\sqrt{2}\right)} ‖a−a∞‖L1​(Ω)2+(3+2​2)​|Ω|2​M1​(9+2​2)​‖b−b∞‖L1​(Ω)2\displaystyle\left\|a-a_{\infty}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}+\frac{\left(3+2\sqrt{2}\right)|\Omega|}{2M_{1}\left(9+2\sqrt{2}\right)}\left\|b-b_{\infty}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}
+(3+2​2)​|Ω|(M1+M2)​(9+2​2)​‖c−c∞‖L1​(Ω)2.\displaystyle+\frac{\left(3+2\sqrt{2}\right)|\Omega|}{\left(M_{1}+M_{2}\right)\left(9+2\sqrt{2}\right)}\left\|c-c_{\infty}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{1}(\Omega)}.

The proof of the above functional inequality is available in [4, Lemma 3.3, p.173] which exploits the conservation properties (4) and (5). ∎

Appendix A some useful results

Lemma 7 (Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality).

There exists a positive constant P⁡(Ω)P(\Omega), depending only on Ω\Omega and qq, such that

P⁡(Ω)​‖∇f‖L2​(Ω)2≥‖f−f¯‖Lq​(Ω)2 for all ​f∈H1​(Ω),P(\Omega)\left\|\nabla f\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{2}(\Omega)}\geq\left\|f-\overline{f}\right\|^{2}_{\mathrm{L}^{q}(\Omega)}\qquad\mbox{ for all }f\in\mathrm{H}^{1}(\Omega),

where

q={2​NN−2 for ​N≥3,∈[1,∞) for ​N=2,∈[1,∞)∪{∞} for ​N=1.q=\left\{\begin{aligned} \frac{2N}{N-2}&\qquad\mbox{ for }\,\,N\geq 3,\\ \in[1,\infty)&\qquad\mbox{ for }\,\,N=2,\\ \in[1,\infty)\cup\{\infty\}&\qquad\mbox{ for }\,\,N=1.\end{aligned}\right.

We refer to P⁡(Ω)P(\Omega) as the Poincaré constant.

Theorem 11 (Second Order Regularity and Integrability estimation).

Let d>0d>0 and let τ∈[0,T)\tau\in[0,T). Take θ∈Lp​(Ωτ,T)\theta\in\mathrm{L}^{p}(\Omega_{\tau,T}) for some 1<p<+∞1<p<+\infty. Let ψ\psi be the solution to the backward heat equation:

{∂tψ+d​Δ​ψ=−θ for (t,x)∈Ωτ,T,∇ψ⋅n⁡(x)=0 for (t,x)∈[τ,T]×∂Ω,ψ⁡(T,x)=0 for x∈Ω.\left\{\begin{aligned} \partial_{t}\psi+d\Delta\psi&=-\theta\qquad\mbox{ for }(t,x)\in\Omega_{\tau,T},\\ \nabla\psi\cdot n(x)&=0\qquad\ \ \mbox{ for }(t,x)\in[\tau,T]\times\partial\Omega,\\ \psi(T,x)&=0\qquad\ \ \mbox{ for }x\in\Omega.\end{aligned}\right.

Then, there exists a positive constant CS​O​RC_{SOR}, depending only on the domain Ω\Omega, the dimension NN and the exponent pp such that the following maximal regularity holds:

(76) ‖Δ​ψ‖Lp​(Ωτ,T)≤CS​O​Rd​‖θ‖Lp​(Ωτ,T).\displaystyle\|\Delta\psi\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}(\Omega_{\tau,T})}\leq\frac{C_{SOR}}{d}\|\theta\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}(\Omega_{\tau,T})}.

Moreover, if θ≥0\theta\geq 0 then ψ⁡(t,x)≥0\psi(t,x)\geq 0 for almost every (t,x)∈Ωτ,T(t,x)\in\Omega_{\tau,T}. Furthermore, we have

If\displaystyle\mbox{If } p=N+22​ then ‖ψ‖Ls​(Ωτ,T)≤CI​E​‖θ‖Lp​(Ωτ,T) for all ​s<∞\displaystyle p=\frac{N+2}{2}\,\mbox{ then }\qquad\left\|\psi\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{s}(\Omega_{\tau,T})}\leq C_{IE}\left\|\theta\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p}(\Omega_{\tau,T})}\qquad\mbox{ for all }\,\,s<\infty

where the constant CI​E=CI​E​(T−τ,Ω,d,p,s)C_{IE}=C_{IE}(T-\tau,\Omega,d,p,s) and
